findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: Observed that the facility did not have sufficient materials to respond to vomiting or diarrheal events - there was not bleach available to make a disinfecting solution, nor was there a bodily fluid cleanup kit. Ensure that the facility can properly disinfect in the event of a bodily fluid contamination event.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed an accumulation of grease and residues on several interior walls of the kitchen. Nonfood-contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Observed the following equipment that is in need of repair or replacement:
(i) The paper towel dispenser in the employee bathroom was not functioning; rolls of paper towels are available on the chemical storage shelf and the dispenser does have paper towels inside of it. The dispenser should be repaired so that employees have better access to paper towels for handwashing.
(ii) The triple sink caulking needs to be repaired, as it is deteriorating and there is an accumulation of soil residues. Repair the caulking so that the area behind the triple sink is sealed and cleanable.
(iii) A ceiling tile above the hot boxes has visible water damage. Replace the ceiling tile, and prevent additional water damage. 
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
3RD REPEAT: Employees working at the time of the inspection could not show proof of food handler certificates. All employees that handle food and are not food manager certified will need to obtain a food handler certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: An opened container of barbecue sauce manufactured by Little Caesars was observed stored at room temperature on a storage rack. The label of the bottle stated to refrigerate after opening. Shown to PIC and the sauce was voluntarily discarded. Ensure to properly follow the label instructions on food packaging to ensure safety of foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The baking sheet pans stored on the storage rack near the pizza line are starting to chip and are no longer in good condition for baking. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that he would purchase new baking sheets soon. Be sure that food contact surfaces are always in good condition and never chipping to ensure the prevention of contaminating food items. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The storage shelf to the right inside of the walk in cooler was observed with a significant amount of dust and other debris. Shown to PIC. When time permits, pull the shelf from the cooler and power-wash or either wipe with a sanitizer towel. Ensure that pieces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
The employee bathroom door is not equipped to close on its own. There is a self-closer located at the top corner of the door but the closer appears to not be functioning properly. Ensure that bathroom doors are tight fitting and self-closing. 

6-202.14: Toilet rooms located on PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with tightfitting and self-closing door.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Cardboard is being used as a mat underneath the triple sink. Discussed with PIC that card board isn't allowed as floor covering. PIC mentioned that the previous mat can’t be located and that the facility will be ordering a new floor mat. Ensure that floor coverings are smooth and easily cleanable. 

Cardboard is also being used as a base layer on a storage rack in the kitchen area. Cardboard isn’t smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that cardboard is never used as a a base layer. 

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

Employees working at the time of inspection could not show proof of food handler certifications. There were food handler certifications in the green folder labeled “health department” but not for employees currently working. Ensure that employees who are not manager certified are food handler certified. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no employee health reporting agreements for the facility. Discussed with PIC. Provided copy for the facility. Ensure all new hires read and sign the document. Ensure all staff has read and signed the document. Inspector will follow-up on 12/21/23.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that facility has a policy. Provided SCDPH’s policy. Ensure facility has bleach to perform procedure.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

(REPEAT) Observed food handling employee to improperly wash hands. Ensure that a barrier is used to turn off the faucet handles. Ensure soap use. Employee rinsed hands quickly and turned off the faucet. Cease practice. Discussed with employee and PIC. Employee re-washed hands. Repeat violation since last routine inspection on 3/21/22. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-702.11: UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. 

Observed the following food contact areas to be in need of cleaning:
1. The prep table next to all the reach-in hot holding units has a significant layer of butter spread all over the prep station, the wall in front of the prep station, and the metal grating of the shelving unit under and next to this area. Area and shelving unit, including the wall, needs cleaned of food splash.
2. The can opener was soiled with old food debris. Employee cleaned during the inspection. COS.
3. The shelving unit that stores the clean dish ware next to the 3 compartment sink is soiled with food splash and debris. Clean dishes are on this shelving unit. Shelving unit needs cleaned.
4. The walk-in cooler shelving units are soiled in a layer of food build-up and debris. Shelving needs cleaned.
5. The pizza dough and bread stick shelving carts in the walk-in cooler have layers of food splash and debris on them. Carts need cleaned. 

Discussed cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to routinely clean these areas. Inspector will follow-up on 12/21/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed all the working sani buckets to be 100 ppm and had lost concentration. Discussed with PIC. PIC remade all 3 buckets. Ensure frequent sani bucket changes in order to maintain a concentration of 200-400 ppm. Facility has test strips to verify. COS.
